old_title: Celebrity Traitors 2026 live: 'Genius' Hannah Fry move sets up tonight's episode
new_title: Celebrity Traitors 2026 live: Much-loved Faithful makes shock roundtable exit

It was the end of the road for Traitor Richard E Grant in the third episode of Celebrity Traitors, with the Oscar nominee ousted before two major plot twists saw a new Traitor recruited and a Faithful banished.
Grant, who was selected by host Claudia Winkleman to be one of two Traitors alongside Maya Jama in the series' first episode, caused waves of suspicion almost immediately last week when he - for slightly inexplicable reasons - declared to Faithful Joe Lycett during a gab in the kitchen that he was, in fact, a Traitor. This ended up getting him banished.
But it wasn't over yet: Maya and fellow Traitor James Acaster decided to recruit Hannah Fry to their side, with Hannah then using her newfound powers to throw suspicion onto Industry star Myha'la. Her fellow stars seemingly took the bait, and Myha'la was banished. We left the series with yet another cliffhanger ending, as Maya, James and Hannah plotted to murder one of the three Faithfuls they've marked for death: Bella Ramsey, Jerry Hall and Sebastian Croft.
Follow along with all the latest Celebrity Traitors updates in our live blog below, with the next episode starting at 8pm on Friday on BBC One.
Why did Myha'la wink at Rchard?
"That was outside of the game, that was just for Richard - it was like, 'You're a kindred spirit, I know you're going to be gone and I'll see you on the other side'."
Richard E Grant explains himself
On Celebrity Traitors: Uncloaked, Richard E Grant tried to explain why he quickly announced that he was a Traitor, and repeated his oft-mentioned excuse that he was just too excited.
Myha'la
Newly banished Myha'la has discovered who the Traitors are - and it's safe to say she was shocked.
Poor Maya Jama
Is anyone else getting the sneaking suspicion that this year's "baddie" Maya Jama is getting fed up with her timid accomplices?
She has herself to blame - Amol Rajan would have quite evidently lapped up the chance to be a Traitor, and she opted for James Acaster instead. And picking Hannah Fry put her in a hell of a position, considering she was up for "murder" - so everyone would naturally think she could've been recruited.
Here's hoping she can bring the evil out of them a little bit in the episodes to come...
Hannah Fry - right or wrong choice for recruitment?
The Traitors had a choice to "murder" Hannah Fry or Jerry Hall, or recruit somebody, and they opted to recruit... Hannah Fry.
"It was a question of kill me or recruit me," Hannah said, acknowledging that she is "the biggest threat" to the existing Traitors.
But was this the right choice? Fans are divided, with some believing they should have chosen another random Faithful who wasn't up for murder.
However, it could be a genius move, considering there's some suspicion on Hannah and Maya Jama and James Acaster would have an easy sacrifice on their hands should they need it...
Who will get 'murdered' tonight?
In the running for "murder" tonight are Bella Ramsey, Sebastian "Bash" Croft and James Blunt.
I'd rule Blunt out considering he's an absolute master at orchestrating tactics during the tasks - a sure-fire way to insure you remain on the show for a while - leaving Bella and Bash.
I think Bash would be the logical choice here because A) he's clearly a Faithful and B) I think it might throw suspicion onto Bella, considering they're close friends and people will think it's a classic attempt at misdirect.
ICYMI: James Blunt has gone viral
James Blunt has somewhat surprisingly become the star of the annual Traitors shower shot.
Myha'la blames Richard E Grant for banishment
Industry star Myha'la became the second celebrity to be banished - and she blames Traitor Richard E Grant for her fate.
"I immediately got close to Richard, just because I feel like we're twin flames. Really, I shouldn't trust him as far as I could throw him, which is ultimately, I think, my demise," she said.
Myha'la added that she's "annoyed" Richard couldn't stay in "because I feel like he could have brought me to the turret and I would have gladly led him to glory".
"There's an alternate universe in which he and I get to the final," the Faithful - who desperately wanted to be a Traitor - said.

Hannah Fry almost became the second Traitor to be banished on Friday (9 October) night - but the maths whizz survived another day thanks to an unsual defence.
The episode began with Bella Ramsey becoming the second Celebrity Traitors star to be murdered, and just as our trio in the turret predicted, their exit sent the Faithfuls into a spin.
Before they reconvened at the roundtable, there was a challenge to deal with and host Claudia Winkleman took the players to the show's infamous cabin (yes, the one where Celia Imrie passed wind). This time, it was Miranda Hart who found herself unable to control her bodily functions - vomiting at the horrendous smell in the wooden hut.
At the roundtable, Hannah made a passionate plea not just for herself but for Julie Hesmondhalgh, who had also raised suspicisions. It was a play that miraculously worked with the Coronation Street str being banished.
We left the series with yet another cliffhanger ending, as the Traitors picked Rob Beckett, Romesh Ranganathan, Leigh-Anne Pinnock and Ross Kemp for a late-night game of hide'n'seek. They will hide in crypts, where one will be murdered face-to-face. What the Traitors don't know, is that Little Mix singer Leigh-Anne has a key that will save her from an attempted murder.
Follow along with all the latest Celebrity Traitors updates in our live blog below...
Forget Maya Jama - this is the best player on Celebrity Traitors right now
Is self-proclaimed "Marple" Miranda Hart secretly the best player on the show right now?
She's certainly leading the charge against Hannah Fry. On Thursday's episode, Hart pointed out that Fry had been economical with the truth about her tussle with Myha'la for a shield during the last challenge.
She then put the pressure back on the mathematician during Friday's round table - although ultimately it was Faithful Julie Hesmondhalgh that was sent home.
For my colleague Lauren Morris, it's these astute detective skills that make Hart perhaps the best Faithful in the game - or even the best player full stop.
You can read her take below. Such fun!
Viewers spot Hannah Fry's big round table mistake that could seal her fate
Professor Hannah Fry came under serious heat from her fellow Celebrity Traitors players during last night (9 October)'s round table - so could a slip-up in her defence speech come back to haunt her?
The mathematician and broadcaster, 42, was recruited as a Traitor by Maya Jama and James Acaster following the early banishment of actor Richard E. Grant.
However she has consistently raised the suspicion of the other players since then, and ended up as one of the top two contenders for banishment during episode four's round table, alongside actor and Coronation Street legend Julie Hesmondhalgh.
Her bold defence speech managed to win over the other celebs - but viewers at home, however, were convinced that a small but significant slip-up made by Fry could end up sealing her fate and bring about her banishment in the not-so-distant future...
How age could be silently influencing Celebrity Traitors decisions
There's a 47-year age gap between the youngest and oldest on this year's series of The Celebrity Traitors, but contestants on each side of the spectrum are having equally as hard a time as the other - and an expert has revealed that there's a reason for that.
It could be argued that being the youngest or eldest of the crop might work in one's favour, but so far, it's just getting them in trouble. Richard E Grant, 69, shot himself in the foot by letting his excitement get the better of him after declaring himself a Traitor to the group moments after Claudia Winkleman made him one. He swiftly got banished.
Then, the group successfully set its banishment sights on 30-year-old Industry star Myha'la, who sat on the younger side of the crop, while many others were casting doubt upon this year's oldest celeb, former model Jerry Hall, 70, who is proving to be equally as chaotic as Grant; she made a wholly innocent outburst at the breakfast table, which in turn confused everyone and has many convinced she's a Traitor.
My colleague Jacob Stolworthy has some pretty astute analysis as ever on why age might end up being a key factor in this year's competition...
A traitorous recap from last night
Good morning Faithfuls! Katie Rosseinsky here, logging on for your post-Traitors morning debrief. In case you need a little recap of what went down in the castle last night, I'm here to oblige.
- First, we learned that the Traitors had cruelly murdered Bella Ramsey, who made a real impression during their brief stint in the castle with their astute eye for suspicious behaviour. Gone far too soon!
- Then, Bella's in-castle pal Julie went absolutely OTT with her response to her mate's death - which certainly raised eyebrows among her fellow players.
- Claudia made an appearance to introduce the next challenge, in which half the group stood around chanting to "summon spirits" while the others scrabbled around in a crypt trying to solve clues. Things got particularly messy when Sebastian stuck his head down a toilet - not a sentence I expected to be writing 24 hours ago.
- At the round table, there were two main contenders for banishment: Faithful Julie and Traitor Hannah.
- The vote ended up in a near draw between the two, but it was Julie who ended up being sent home. Bless her, she was getting really, really into it.
- In another twist, the Traitors were then tasked with choosing four Faithfuls to take part in a creepy hide and seek game, in which they'll have the chance to murder one of them face to face.
- Ross, Romesh, Rob and Leigh-Anne were the unlikely quartet they picked - but the latter was given a special key that will protect her from murder, should the Traitors attempt to kill her off.
How the face-to-face murder will work
We're not even halfway through the series and the second face-to-face murder is about to take place!
The Traitors were asked to choose four celebrities who would enter crypts - and for once, they haven't chosen to put any of their own in the game.
Instead, it's Ross, Rob, Romesh and Leigh-Anne who have been summoned by Claudia in the middle of the night.
Before being placed in the crypts, the foursome have decided who to award a special key to. The key will grant that player immunity from murder, and they've gone for Leigh-Anne.
So if the Traitors decide to kill her, all four of the celebs in crypts will survive...
Traitors' cabin delivers another jaw-dropping moment
Last year, we had Celia Imrie passing wind. And this year, poor Miranda *checks notes* threw up into a toilet. Not such fun!
Appearing on Uncloaked, Julie was asked about Hannah's decision to defend her at the roundtable - while being under fire herself.
"It worked, didn't it?" Julie said. "Everyone was gunning for Hannah, then turned on me. I think it was the fact I got that shield [at the start].
"As I said several times, I thought I'd chosen the next Traitor."
Asked who she would have given the second shield to, if she hadn't kept it for herself back in episode one, Julie said Hannah. I wonder if that would have changed the game at all?
I have to say, Jerry's transformation from the most oblivious person in the castle to the only person who has clocked James Acaster is jaw-dropping.
Is it more luck than judgment? Probably. But it's impressive nonetheless.
Watch: Most trusted Faithful to banished...
Poor Julie!
Here's the moment when she left the game...
